analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The single changed range is head line 2371: a new failure-mode table row about cold loads being refused (503 or insufficient-memory) while an idle model is resident under an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. The row cites ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel, autopilotHeldWeightBytes and ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift. The supplied units are base text only (lines 803-1617), and the changed line falls outside them. I could not view the head-side row text beyond the patch excerpt. The change is documentation only and alters no code, so it has no direct security impact. Nothing in the changed text touches the A-001 prompt data, key material, attestation/App Attest authorization (TB-011) or the cache storage threat T-041; the cache and prefix-cache text in the base units is unchanged.

Open question for later passes: the documented Autopilot hold behavior comes from code outside this batch. Holds exclude slots from eviction and withhold the free_for_load_gb reclaim credit, which could affect availability or the DoS posture of TB-007 and T-029. A provider could stay unable to cold-load another model while a hold persists. The hold's expiry and authority (whether the coordinator or an operator can place it) are not visible here, so I cannot assess them. If the code change comes in another batch, check that the hold is bounded and authenticated, and that it does not extend into App Attest serving authorization. No threat-model gap is evident from the docs line alone.
